draft.title: Christian ethics
card: Christian ethics is the set of ideas about right and wrong that Christians draw from the Bible and Jesus's teaching. Three sources guide it.
Ten Commandments
a list of commands given to Moses in the Hebrew scriptures. They cover duties to God, such as worshipping only God, and duties to others, such as not murdering, stealing or lying.
Beatitudes
blessings spoken by Jesus in the Sermon on the Mount. They name attitudes such as being merciful, humble and a peacemaker, and say these people are blessed.
Love command
Jesus said the greatest commands are to love God and to love your neighbour as yourself. Many Christians see this as the heart of Christian ethics.
draft.remember: Christian ethics draws on the Ten Commandments, the Beatitudes and the command to love God and neighbour.

a.q: Which source of Christian ethics names attitudes such as mercy and peacemaking and says people who have them are blessed?
opts: The Beatitudes
The Ten Commandments
The love command
The Sermon on the Mount's parables
a.why: The Beatitudes are blessings from Jesus that praise attitudes such as mercy and peacemaking. The Ten Commandments are a list of commands about duties, not blessings on attitudes.

b.q: Sam says Christians should not steal because the Ten Commandments forbid it. Priya says Christians should help a stranger in need because Jesus taught love of neighbour. Which statement is correct?
opts: Each uses a different source of Christian ethics
Both rely on the Beatitudes
Both use the Ten Commandments
Only Priya uses a source that comes from Jesus
b.why: Sam uses the Ten Commandments and Priya uses the command to love your neighbour, so they draw on different sources. The last option is tempting, but the card does not say the other sources are not part of Christian ethics, and Sam's source is still one that guides Christians.
b.clue: Match each person's reason to one of the three sources.

b.best: Each uses a different source of Christian ethics
also_right: Only Priya uses a source that comes from Jesus

a.q: How do the Beatitudes differ from the Ten Commandments?
opts: They bless attitudes rather than list commands
They were given to Moses rather than spoken by Jesus
They cover duties to God rather than duties to others
They forbid acts such as murder, stealing and lying
a.why: The Beatitudes say people with attitudes such as mercy are blessed, while the Ten Commandments are a list of commands. It was the Ten Commandments, not the Beatitudes, that were given to Moses and that forbid murder, stealing and lying.
a.clue: Think about what the word blessed tells you.

b.q: Sam says Christians should not lie because it is one of the commands given to Moses. Priya says Christians should show mercy to a stranger because Jesus said the merciful are blessed. Which sources do they use?
opts: Sam uses the Ten Commandments, Priya the Beatitudes
Sam uses the Ten Commandments, Priya the love command
Sam uses the Beatitudes, Priya the love command
Sam uses the love command, Priya the Ten Commandments
b.why: Commands given to Moses are the Ten Commandments, and saying the merciful are blessed is a Beatitude. Helping a stranger sounds like loving your neighbour, but Priya's reason is a blessing on an attitude, which points to the Beatitudes.
b.clue: Look at the reason each person gives, not the action.
